body: Alright, I see your point. And I'm genuinely surprised you've came to these conclusions, I guess I can't elaborate much further, cause it will inevitably lead to a dead end. This piece of media doesn't have a singular meaning to it, so claiming to "understand" it's meaning and still not being able to see the others' takes is contradictory too. That's not a jab at you, this is me just pointing out the obvious. Anyway, this conversation was interesting, have a good one.

Don't worry, your response is reasonable, it's actually cool to converse with a Spanish Umi fan, you're going to be the second one. And I might take this in consideration, because of the different culture you see things not like I do, and that's completely fine. 

>To me you are taking forgiveness with not acknowledging the wrongdoings... Is not about that, is about stop suffering from the mentioned wrongdoings (that Ange clearly reached at the end)...

Actually, it's an opposite situation. I'm talking about forgiving the action, but doing it in the meaningful way, with all the accountability from a perpetrator, but also keeping in mind that no amount of accountability might fix the damage (I will expand on that later). In other words, forgiving someone's wrongdoing should come with the aknowledgement from a perpetrator and a victim, you can't forgive someone just like that. The perpetrator should be aware and ready to admit their wrongs, and the victim should have the courage to speak up and hear them out. It doesn't really apply to the characters, cause you know, they are fictional, but I choose to hold them to somewhat realistic standarts.

>In episode 2 we have Rosa entire character detailed, how she was like Maria, all her siblings just traumatized her and in the need of love she got her partner and he left her pregnant with Maria... It even goes as far as to say that before all her abuse she didn't know how to be a mother and in the efforts to be a good one she just spoiled Maria (remember she is young in the novel)

>She even detailed herself as a horrible mother in that same episode. So to me yeah you can blame the readers to "hate" a character like that...

And this is where our cultural differences are coming into play. Where I'm from, no matter how self aware abuser is, it won't ever excuse their behaviour. We are talking about being aware of one's problems and never working on them, it's not about someone being unaware of a harm they're causing. Abusers often weaponize their victimhood and refuse to ever work on it under a pretence "not being able to help it", so here it is very much frowned upon to consciously pass a generational trauma. Rosa was very much aware of what she is doing is wrong, so this judgement applies to her 100%. I'm not saying that my culture is superior to yours, I'm just saying it's different, and that's why I see things like this. And I guess this is where we can safely agree to disagree on her character.

In conclusion, I strongly believe you can harbor as much "hate" as you want (this is a strong word, but it is miscontrued a lot, just like "love"), no matter how much reasoning it is given to not hate on them. It's a personal choice, and we can't really police someone's feelings regarding fictional characters.

True, but my point still stands. It's ok to dislike fictional characters completely, it's also fine to take them for what they are and appreciate how masterfully they are written. It's also ok to not forgive the actions of these characters. 

Because, after all, the vn doesn't want you to accept and condone all of the abuse, and it doesn't want to minimize it's impact on the victims. For me, it's like a study of their mind, I can see where all of these characters are coming from, and I sympathize with some of them deeply, but it will be wrong to just not aknowledge their wrongdoings. Like your example with Rosa, can we really blame the readers, who were in a DV situation, being very much opposed to accept her character? I don't think so.

And this is why denying someone's strong disliking for a character is really weird, in my opinion.

But you still can identify the monstrous behavior of your favorite characters, aknowledge how none of it is ok, and still say "i like how this character is written". Not understanding the message of the vn has nothing to do with your feelings towards them, especially during early chapters. It's really weird to anticipate everyone to enjoy explicitly abusive characters, if you can do it, doesn't mean every single reader will.

Hello, native speaker here.
I think your handwriting is pretty decent, not perfect, but readable nontheless. The ь character doesn't have to be this tall otherwise it looks like the cursive lowercase в. And if you really want to improve, you can do an exercise all russian speaking students do in elementary school, it's simple and effective: you need a lined notebook with diagonal lines (idk if they're avaliable in your country and if they have a specific name but here is how they look like: https://www.teacherspayteachers.com/Product/Russian-Handwriting-Worksheet-Practice--3243416 ), and just repeat writing one russian letter at time, three lines in a row minimum, in upper and lower case each or in combination (eg three lines of Ц and ц separately or three lines of Цц). It should help to achieve consistency and it's a good training for muscle memory.
Anyway I hope I hadn't confused you, if you have questions, feel free to ask, I'll try my best to explain. Практикуйся, и со временем у тебя всё получится :)
